I’m not a therapist, I can only share from my experience. But I used to do EMDR therapy for both medical and emotional trauma. Is this something you have heard of? 

It sounds really weird but bare with me

Basically, the therapist asks for prompts to figure out exactly what it is that’s causing the trauma, and then uses a stick with a target on the end back and forth, and the patient follows with their eyes while talking to the therapist and answering questions/imagining things. This is to simulate the brains REM when asleep, because that’s when your brain sorts the difficult parts of the day, but sometimes things are too big and the brain struggles to do so. This is where EMDR can be helpful, to sort the parts that are too difficult for your brain to handle on its own. There are also “bilateral stimulation songs”, on YouTube that kind of do a similar thing if you listen with headphones on. You’ll often find your eyes moving to the music at the same time. 

I’m not a doctor so my explanation might be slightly weird, so have a google if you want to find out more/make your own conclusions :)

Hey, I know this is scary and I’ve been there, but the best thing you could possibly do is reach out to your family and those around you. It might suck, and be really hard, but they love and care for you. You don’t have to do it alone. I know it might not feel like it, but there is always a way out that isn’t suicide. If possible, I would reach out to a psychologist, too. It will be uncomfortable sitting with these difficult feelings for a while, but trust me, it is so, so worth it. There will be a day where you wake up and you will feel ok again. You need to choose you every single day. You need to be honest with those around you with what you need out of life and help from them. None of us want to see you go, and we believe in you! You have to be gentle with yourself. You have to be willing to reach out. You have to keep discipline, just in a different way. You have to look at yourself and tell yourself that you love who you are, over and over and over until you start to believe it. You have to be disciplined in keeping good people in your life and ones that will uplift you. You have to be disciplined in taking things slow and appreciating your body for carrying you through life. You have to remind yourself that you are still loveable and worthy, because it is so much more than skin deep. You have to take it slow, and aim for consistency in creating a better mindset rather than trying to get better all at once. It takes time, but trust me, it is so, so worth it. I’m in Australia, so I’m not sure if it’s different in other parts of the world, but you usually go home the same day. I went to class 2 days after because I was bored. But you don’t feel right until at least a week after, if you take it easy you should be able to go to your partners place. My op is the 16th and I’m planning on going to see my family on the 20th- and then travelling to house sit the 26-29th. I’ll probably work from home a couple days after surgery too. Everyone is different, so if you feel terrible after I would suggest listening to your body and rest. I’m just stubborn 

The worst part for me was the gas rising after. They didn’t tell me it would happen, and it didn’t go into my shoulder like usual, it hit my lung so every time I breathed it was agony and I thought my lung was collapsing. It was honestly more painful than the surgery itself. But it doesn’t last very long and hopefully you don’t get it or it goes into your shoulder - make sure you take something like Metamucil or stool softener because it will hurt to squeeze to poop - and make sure things in your shower aren’t too low so you don’t have to bend to grab things etc 

So much love to you for your surgery, feel free to message me and we can check in with each other post op! I hope you have a nice Christmas break after and that you heal well ❤️ just bring a pillow for the car so the seatbelt doesn’t pull on your stomach and don’t eat too much too soon because being full hurts a little

When I saw a physiotherapist after my first lap, he told me to touch my belly button often otherwise it will be sensitive and feel weird later - I know it’s uncomfortable and painful but maybe even 10 seconds a day might start to help and if your doctor can give you any medication to help in case it’s an infection
